title: How to Drive Impulse Purchases In-Store | Entuned
meta_description: Strategies to increase impulse buying in retail stores, including how music and sound prime spontaneous purchase decisions.

faq.q: What percentage of retail purchases are impulse buys?
faq.a: Studies suggest that the majority of in-store buying decisions are unplanned. For small-format specialty retailers, these add-on purchases can meaningfully shift daily revenue without requiring any additional foot traffic.

faq.q: What is the connection between music and impulse buying?
faq.a: Impulse buying is arousal-driven. Moderate-to-uptempo music with major keys and bright production increases physiological arousal, elevates mood, and shifts decision-making from deliberative ('do I need this?') to intuitive ('I want this'). That shift is exactly what impulse purchasing requires.

faq.q: What is the ideal music tempo for encouraging impulse purchases?
faq.a: The sweet spot for most specialty retail is 95-120 BPM, major key, medium energy, with positive lyrical themes. Below that range the environment feels too calm for impulse behavior. Above it, customers feel rushed rather than inspired.

faq.q: Why does novelty in store music matter for impulse buying?
faq.a: Novelty contributes to arousal. A customer who's heard the same background music on their last three visits has stopped noticing it. A customer hearing something fresh is in a more alert, engaged state, and that alertness transfers to product attention and willingness to grab the add-on item.
